the steady summer north wind of the Aegean
the north-easterly wind: when it blows, swim the south coast
the south-westerly wind: when it blows, cross to the north and east
a tavern of meze and rakı, the long evening table
the small plates that come out in waves before and with the fish
the anise spirit drunk with water and the meze
small hand-pinched dumplings, sauced with yoghurt and chilli butter
tomato jam, the island’s best-known preserve
the Greek Orthodox community of Anatolia and the islands
a holy spring, from the Greek hagiasma
the grape harvest, and the island’s harvest festival
the island’s white grape, eaten fresh and made into dry white wine
the island’s other white grape, crisp and high in acid
the island’s dark, tannic red grape
a shared minibus that leaves when it is full
winemaking: the word on a winery’s sign
the Greek name of Gökçeada, the other island of the treaty
bluefish, the autumn fish of the straits
Atlantic bonito, running through the straits in autumn
